* For simplicity the majority of compiler passes do not treat hooks specially. However, hooks are different
* from regular functions in two key ways:
* - They can introduce reactivity even when their arguments are non-reactive (accounted for in InferReactivePlaces)
* - It can access context, and therefore introduce reactivity
* - It can be called conditionally, but _it must be called if the component needs the return value_. This is because
*   React uses the fact that use was called to remember that the component needs the value, and that changes to the
*   input should invalidate the component itself.
* This pass accounts for the "can't call conditionally" aspect of both hooks and use. Though the reasoning is slightly
* different for reach, the result is that we can't memoize scopes that call hooks or use since this would make them
* The pass finds and removes any scopes that transitively contain a hook or use call. By running all
* the reactive scope inference first, agnostic of hooks, we know that the reactive scopes accurately
* describe the set of values which "construct together", and remove _all_ that memoization in order
* to ensure the hook call does not inadvertently become conditional.

content.title: React Compiler: an eight-file way in
content.summary: Eight compiler files from the real 3,669-file change. Explore the entry point, gating, pipeline and dependency boundaries. Source and cited relationships come from the original run; download that run for the complete map.

annotations.title: 1. Entry, eligibility, emission and gating
annotations.text: The Babel Program visitor parses options and invokes compileProgram. File/function directives, source selection, existing cache imports and compilation modes control eligibility. Gating chooses a compiled or original function and can change declaration hoisting.

annotations.title: 2. HIR, control flow and SSA
annotations.text: Lowering converts Babel functions to HIR. The pipeline normalizes blocks, checks identifiers and successors, enters SSA and removes redundant phis. SSA makes definitions explicit across joins and loop back edges before inference.

annotations.title: 3. Types, effects, aliases and mutable lifetimes
annotations.text: Type inference unifies equations; reference-effect inference distinguishes read, mutation, freezing and immutable values using React assumptions. Mutable-range inference repeatedly refines store/phi aliases before reactive-scope construction.

annotations.title: 5. Construct-together scopes and hook flattening
annotations.text: Reactive scopes group mutable values that construct or mutate together, align to structured control flow and merge overlaps. Hooks and use introduce a later constraint: scopes transitively containing them are flattened to preserve required calls.

annotations.title: 6. Dependencies, conditional reads and safe invalidation
annotations.text: Dependency propagation includes non-stable values created before a scope and propagates inner dependencies upward. Minimal dependency derivation may shorten property paths so every emitted dependency check is safe to read unconditionally.
